EFW_OlyriaTrench.name: Olyria-Prime Trench
EFW_OlyriaTrench.text: Working excavation cut into black bedrock on Olyria-Prime; heavy drills, work lamps, dust, ladders, shift gear and tired crews. Keep figures readable against the dark industrial environment with deliberate warm work-light separation, reflective surfaces and controlled atmospheric depth rather than uniform low-value murk.

EFW_ZenithArchives.name: Zenith Spire Archives
EFW_ZenithArchives.text: Institutional archive high in Zenith Spire; ordered shelves, old ledgers, current records, secure desks and long views over the planet. Use a brighter controlled architectural field behind characters so silhouettes separate clearly; Rae's dark practical styling should read immediately against ordered pale/cool institutional surfaces.

EFW_SectorFour.name: Sector Four Excavation
EFW_SectorFour.text: Newly opened excavation section where the Desert Marker emerges from black bedrock amid work platforms, dust and temporary lighting. The Marker is ancient, dark and deliberate; use focused work lights and reflected edge light so Theo, Vark and the object remain distinct instead of merging into one dark mass.

EFW_GridRuins.name: Stabilizing Grid Ruins
EFW_GridRuins.text: Damaged excavation tier after the first memory rupture, with broken platforms, dust, abandoned tools and stunned workers. Preserve the established Olyria palette but separate foreground figures from wreckage through directional practical light and atmospheric falloff.

EFW_TelemetryRoom.name: Zenith Telemetry Room
EFW_TelemetryRoom.text: Secure Zenith records room with controlled access, workstations, archive terminals and institutional oversight. Interfaces are functional evidence, not generic holographic decoration. Keep backgrounds cleaner and brighter than Rae's silhouette; preserve Caelum's lighter formal styling as a distinct second value family.

EFW_TriageTent.name: Olyria Triage Tent
EFW_TriageTent.text: Temporary field medical tent with cots, paper forms, ordinary supplies, tired workers and bad coffee. Human-scale, practical, comparatively brighter than the trench; let faces, bandaged hand, paper incident form and small acting beats read clearly without cinematic murk.

EFW_LowerArchives.name: Lower-Tier Archives
EFW_LowerArchives.text: Older archive stacks beneath the polished public levels, filled with physical books, sealed records and infrequently used storage rooms. Dimmer than the upper archive but not muddy: use localized pools of readable light, pale paper/stone/metal surfaces and depth separation around Rae and Adrian.

EFW_ObservationDeck.name: Zenith Observation Deck
EFW_ObservationDeck.text: High-altitude observation deck overlooking Zenith Spire and the planet below, with quiet public space and ordinary disposal infrastructure. Use the luminous exterior/city/planet view as controlled negative space so Rae and Caelum stand out cleanly in silhouette and facial value.

EFW_AbandonedTrench.name: Abandoned Trench
EFW_AbandonedTrench.text: Shut-down excavation cut with sparse work lights, scrap, deep shadow and enough loose material to conceal the reopened site. Dark environment, but preserve facial readability and the industrial cutter through selective practical light, rim separation and uncluttered staging.

EFW_CompactedEarth.name: Compacted Earth Above Sector Four
EFW_CompactedEarth.text: Surface above buried Sector Four beneath silent excavators and open stars, exposed and still after the work crews leave. Night scene with clear moon/star/industrial edge separation; Theo, Adrian and the small Marker fragment must remain readable without bathing the page in generic glow.

EFW_NuxisArchive.name: Nuxis Archive Room
EFW_NuxisArchive.text: Quiet present-day archive room with ordinary shelves, paper records, a sealed rain-streaked window and subdued city light. Small, practical and non-mystical; memory intrusion should feel disproportionate to the modest room.

EFW_DesertMarkerWarRoom.name: Desert Marker War Room
EFW_DesertMarkerWarRoom.text: Worn ancient command room close to the civilian line, with practical tables, maps, open doors, dust blowing in and evacuation noise always intruding. It should never feel sealed away from the people affected by decisions made inside.

EFW_DesertMarkerRidge.name: Desert Marker Ridge
EFW_DesertMarkerRidge.text: Exposed ridge above the Desert Marker basin with direct views toward settlement, evacuation routes, damaged territory and the destabilizing sky. Use the landscape to make strategic arguments physically legible.

EFW_DesertMarkerBattlefield.name: Desert Marker Battlefield
EFW_DesertMarkerBattlefield.text: Open ancient battlefield at the point where containment and decisive action collide. Civilian routes remain visible at the margins; dust, fractured terrain and the failing sky provide scale. Preserve Redlin's proximity to people and Starbreaker's elevated strike geometry.

EFW_DesertMarkerAftermath.name: Desert Marker Aftermath
EFW_DesertMarkerAftermath.text: The same basin immediately after the rupture: glass dust, violet light, silence, injured survivors and visibly altered physical reality. Aftermath first, spectacle second.

EFW_VaelTorPublicArchive.name: Vael-Tor Public Archive
EFW_VaelTorPublicArchive.text: Civic archive overlooking active transit platforms, with current maps and records layered over much older stonework. Public, busy and practical; the old city appears through reused foundations and map discrepancies rather than a secret mystical chamber.

EFW_VaelTorLandingField.name: Vael-Tor Landing Field
EFW_VaelTorLandingField.text: Working civilian arrival and emergency landing field in hard rain, surrounded by port staff, service vehicles, shelters and ordinary infrastructure. The buried dreadnought may become visible behind it, but refugees and workers remain the human scale reference.

EFW_VaelTorDreadnoughtRecords.name: Vael-Tor Dreadnought Records Room
EFW_VaelTorDreadnoughtRecords.text: Repurposed records space inside the exposed ancient hull, now filled with ordinary archival boxes, worn paper, catalog labels and personal effects handled by present-day workers who do not understand their provenance.

EFW_PaxTreatyChamber.name: Pax-Aeterna Treaty Chamber
EFW_PaxTreatyChamber.text: Severe civic chamber centered on a black human-scale treaty table, with open doors toward evacuation routes and city noise. Ancient political decisions remain physically adjacent to public consequence. In present-day memory reprises, preserve exact table, chair and camera geometry.

EFW_PaxPublicGallery.name: Pax-Aeterna Public Gallery
EFW_PaxPublicGallery.text: Broad civic gallery immediately outside the treaty chamber where evacuation traffic, stalled departures, families and official decisions collide. Keep political crisis embedded in public movement.

EFW_TyrellisCouncilRoom.name: Tyrellis Council Room
EFW_TyrellisCouncilRoom.text: Small tired negotiation room in the ancient waystation: ordinary table, used cups, papers and few remaining staff. The room should make exhaustion and interpersonal pressure more visible than authority.

EFW_TyrellisArchive.name: Tyrellis Municipal Archive
EFW_TyrellisArchive.text: Present-day paper-heavy municipal archive beneath the museum, built directly into older masonry. Reused bindings, handwritten corrections and ordinary storage make physical historical continuity visible without spectacle.

EFW_TyrellisTransitPlatform.name: Tyrellis Transit Platform
EFW_TyrellisTransitPlatform.text: Ordinary working transit platform with departure boards, public-address equipment, service benches, staff radios and constant commuter flow. Memory return happens inside a functioning workplace, not a sealed experiment.

EFW_NeoVectraPlaza.name: Neo-Vectra Transit Plaza
EFW_NeoVectraPlaza.text: Busy modern transit/civic plaza used for commuting, testimony exchange, mutual aid and public gathering as memory spreads. Family photos, work badges, food, forms and recovered symbols coexist; ancient identity is only one layer of present social life.

EFW_NeoVectraMeroStaffRoom.name: Ancient Neo-Vectra Mero Staff Room
EFW_NeoVectraMeroStaffRoom.text: Human-scale wartime staff room used by Mero and junior personnel, with papers, route lists, half-finished drinks and exhausted people moving in and out. It should feel like work, not a council throne room.

EFW_NeoVectraArbiterWorkroom.name: Ancient Neo-Vectra Arbiter Workroom
EFW_NeoVectraArbiterWorkroom.text: Practical triage workroom where Arbiter and Rae turn names, sectors and evacuation capacity into decisions. Records, handwritten corrections and route sheets must remain physically present so language and consequence stay connected.

EFW_NeoVectraBarrier.name: Neo-Vectra South-Gate Access Barrier
EFW_NeoVectraBarrier.text: Temporary present-day pedestrian control point installed on an ordinary civic route near the remembered south-gate footprint. Municipal lists, movable barriers and diverted commuters make the danger administrative rather than militarized.

EFW_CoreForgeCouncil.name: Core-Forge Final Council Chamber
EFW_CoreForgeCouncil.text: Plain ancient chamber chosen because no faction owns it. Worn table, practical seating, open access to adjacent corridors and visibly exhausted participants. Avoid ceremonial grandeur; this is a last meeting among people who have run out of good options.

EFW_CoreForgeCentral.name: Core-Forge Central Scar Chamber
EFW_CoreForgeCentral.text: Present-day central chamber where repaired modern construction intersects the physical scar left by the Reset. Split floor, reused masonry and imperfect seams remain materially legible. No abstract energy-machine aesthetic unless a page explicitly requires an active gesture.

EFW_CoreForgeCorridor.name: Core-Forge Convergence Corridor
EFW_CoreForgeCorridor.text: Shared corridor geometry existing in both ancient and present timelines, with enough unchanged architecture to support precise matched camera positions, body placement and threshold recognition.

EFW_CoreForgeObservation.name: Core-Forge Observation Window
EFW_CoreForgeObservation.text: Quiet present-day observation space after the immediate crisis, built around a broad view of the familiar sky. Human silhouettes and the missing-star field should read cleanly without interface clutter.
